prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_A:
Summary of key proposals and commitments (ideology-neutral)

Health and care
- NHS: Extra £8bn in first year, rising to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years. Reduce waiting lists; rapid GP access; universal NHS dentistry with new contract and investment rising to £3bn/yr by 2030. Primary care: +£1.5bn/yr by 2030 and £2bn capital. Public health: +£1.5bn to restore 2015/16 levels. National Cancer Plan; mental health therapy within 28 days; school counsellor in every primary, secondary and sixth-form college. Assisted dying with safeguards. End new HIV transmissions by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; £20bn/yr investment; national pay/career structure; visa reforms to prevent exploitation; “Gloria’s Law” for essential care supporters. Disability: +5% to disability benefits; oppose PIP voucher plans; SEND transport rights. Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils; extended staying-put.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes a year; end Right to Buy; bring empty homes into use. Renters: local rent controls, end Section 21, long-term leases, energy improvement rights. Retrofit: £29bn for home insulation, £4bn for public buildings, £9bn low-carbon heating, £7bn heat-adaptation (first five years). New homes: Passivhaus-equivalent; solar and heat pumps; planning to require whole-life carbon assessment; protect green spaces/Green Belt.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end subsidies; carbon tax starting £120/t rising to £500/t within 10 years. Targets: wind ~70% of power by 2030; 80 GW offshore, 53 GW onshore, 100 GW solar by 2035. End de-facto onshore wind ban; expand grid, storage and interconnectors; support green hydrogen for industry. Community ownership minimum thresholds. Cease new nuclear; phase out existing over time; regulate biofuels; end imported biomass subsidies.

Economy, work and welfare
- Green investment average £40bn/yr (energy, retrofit, rail, public transport, active travel, industry, water/sewage, nationalisations). Public ownership: rail, water, Big 5 energy retailers. Regional mutual banks (£10bn capital) and £2bn/yr local grants to help SMEs decarbonise. R&D +£30bn over five years; circular economy and right-to-repair measures.
- Work: Repeal anti-union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15/h minimum wage with small-business offset; 10:1 pay ratio; day‑one rights; gig workers classed as workers; move towards four‑day week.
- Welfare: +£40/wk to UC/legacy benefits; end five‑week wait; scrap two‑child cap; +5% disability benefits; maintain pension uprating; +10% carers allowance; scrap bedroom tax; end sanctions; long‑term UBI.

Tax and public finances
- Wealth tax: 1% >£10m, 2% >£1bn. Align CGT and investment income with earnings tax/NICs; remove NI upper earnings limit; equalise pension tax relief to basic rate; reform inheritance tax. Property tax steps toward Land Value Tax; revalue council tax; adjust business rates reliefs. Windfall taxes (oil/gas, banks); VAT cuts for hospitality/arts; higher VAT on private education/financial services. Tackle avoidance; borrow to invest.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; protect 30% land/sea by 2030; nationalise water; DEFRA +£1.5bn; Clean Air Act; Right to Roam; peatland rewetting; woodland +50%; urban biodiversity measures; fully protected MPAs. Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports; end factory farming practices (cages, routine antibiotics), lead ammo and snares; stricter companion animal rules.
- Food/farming: Nearly triple farm support for nature-friendly farming; link payments to reduced pesticides; expand horticulture and mixed farming; free school meals for all and breakfast clubs to Y6; food education; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator; boost domestic horticulture.

Education
- Schools: +£8bn incl. £2bn teacher pay; £2.5bn/yr for safe buildings (RAAC, maintenance); reduce high‑stakes testing; move academies to LA control; VAT on private school fees; SEND +£5bn; school nurses and counsellors. FE/skills: £12bn; sixth form +£3bn; restore EMA. HE: scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; work towards addressing graduate debt.

Transport
- Operating subsidies up to £10bn/yr by 2030; £19bn capital over five years; nationalise rail; local bus control; £2.5bn/yr active travel; oppose new roads; restore fuel duty escalator; road pricing; end new ICE sales by 2027 and ICE road use by 2035; EV scrappage rising to £5bn/yr; default 20 mph in built-up areas. Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; ban short‑haul flights where rail <3h; no airport expansion; apply carbon tax to kerosene.

Democracy, rights, migration, culture, digital
- Fair Politics Act: repeal voter ID; proportional representation; state funding rules; transparency on lobbying/think tanks; votes at 16; replace Lords with elected chamber; £5bn/yr more for English local government; defend HRA/ECHR; scrap restrictive protest laws; self‑ID for trans; X passports.
- Migration: end hostile environment and NRPF; safe routes; right to work for asylum seekers; simplify/at‑cost visas; free NHS for visa holders; remove income requirements; voting rights for visa‑holders; create Department of Migration.
- Arts/media/digital: £5bn over five years for local arts/sport; VAT‑free cultural tickets; media ownership cap (20%); implement Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation; creator IP protection.

Justice and policing
- End routine stop and search and facial recognition; restorative justice; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; MoJ +£11bn over parliament; tackle court backlog; misogyny as hate crime; fund VAWG services; decriminalise sex work; youth services restored; decriminalise personal possession of drugs with diversion.

Foreign policy
- Support Ukraine; work towards EU re‑entry (Customs Union first, free movement, Erasmus). Israel/Palestine: immediate bilateral ceasefire; recognise Palestine; end UK arms exports to Israel; support war‑crimes investigations. Aid to 1% GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI incl. Loss & Damage; ecocide law; debt relief. Sign TPNW; cancel Trident; advocate NATO no‑first‑use and greater emphasis on diplomacy.

TEXT_E:
Summary of key policies in the Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 (ideological framing removed)

- Economy and tax: Industrial strategy focused on green growth and skills; repair UK–EU trade links; responsible fiscal rules to reduce debt share; priority future tax cut via higher personal allowance; new/changed taxes including reversing bank tax cuts, Digital Services Tax at 6%, fairer capital gains, 4% levy on FTSE-100 buybacks, and a proper one-off windfall tax on oil and gas; expand British Business Bank; national financial inclusion strategy.

- Business, jobs and work: Abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; R&D to 3% of GDP by 2030; AI regulation promoting innovation and accountability; stronger late-payment enforcement; skills and training levy replacing apprenticeship levy; apprentices paid at least the minimum wage; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants (aim £10,000); new “dependent contractor” status with basic rights; stronger sick pay; Worker Protection Enforcement Authority.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; 10-year home energy upgrade (free insulation/heat pumps for low-income households), social energy tariff, zero‑carbon standard for new buildings, decouple power prices from gas; no fracking or new coal; expand storage and interconnectors; support community energy; carbon border adjustment; associate UK ETS with EU ETS.

- Health: Right to see a GP within 7 days (24 hours if urgent), 8,000 more GPs, expanded pharmacist roles and 24/7 booking; urgent NHS dentistry access and contract reform; mental health hubs for young people, routine mental health check-ups, a professional in every school; cancer treatment to start within 62 days; 10‑year estates plan; ambulance delay reductions; digital upgrades; drug policy shift including regulated cannabis market.

- Social care and carers: Free personal care; workforce plan, Royal College of Care Workers, and a Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); cross‑party funding commission; paid carer’s leave and guaranteed respite; National Care Agency and portable care packages; kinship care support.

- Education and families: Per‑pupil funding to rise in real terms; repair school estates; tutoring guarantee; early years boost (extra free hours and tripled premium for disadvantaged children); maintenance grants restored; teacher workforce strategy and funded CPD; SEND reforms and funding; return to Erasmus+; parental leave/pay as day‑one rights, doubled statutory pay, extra month for partners; extend free school meals to all children in poverty.

- Welfare and pensions: Scrap benefit cap and two-child limit; cut Universal Credit wait to 5 days; replace sanctions with incentive-based support; protect triple lock; fair compensation for 1950s-born women; raise and widen Carer’s Allowance; disability benefit and assessment reforms; Independent Living Taskforce.

- Crime and justice: Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance/investigation for all burglaries; clear court backlogs; improve rehabilitation; domestic abuse specialists; Online Crime Agency; replace PCCs with local Police Boards; youth diversion nationwide; stronger fraud reimbursement; modern slavery protections; prison officer recruitment and resettlement plan.

- Nature and water: Turn water companies into public benefit companies; ban bonuses until leaks/discharges end; new tougher regulator, sewage tax, real-time discharge data; binding nature targets (including tree planting 60m/year), expand protected areas; Clean Air Act and new agency; deposit return scheme; phase out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics within three years; peatland and marine restoration.

- Food and farming: National Food Strategy; accelerate and fund ELMS (+£1bn/year); veterinary/plant health agreements with EU; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator; support local abattoirs and sustainable procurement; fisheries sustainability; animal welfare bill, ban caged hens; bTB vaccines; fund alternative proteins.

- Housing and homelessness: 380,000 homes/year including 150,000 social; 10 new garden cities; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; ban no‑fault evictions, 3‑year default tenancies, national landlord register; councils able to end Right to Buy; remove dangerous cladding at no cost to leaseholders; Rent to Own; plan to end rough sleeping and repeal Vagrancy Act; stronger controls on second homes/short lets.

- Local government and connectivity: Multi‑year settlements; more local powers including on second homes; gigabit broadband nationwide; rural support (post office hubs, fuel duty relief); bus franchising powers.

- Transport: Rapid EV charging rollout, restore plug‑in grant, cut VAT on public charging to 5%, 2030 zero‑emission new car/van sales; freeze rail fares, simplify ticketing; major rail electrification, Northern Powerhouse Rail, review HS2 north; £2 bus fare cap and expansion; integrated ticketing; active travel networks; shift freight to rail; curb frequent-flyer emissions, tax private jets, ban short domestic flights with <2.5h rail alternative; airport expansion moratorium.

- Culture, media and sport: Protect public service broadcasters; Creative Europe participation; simple EU touring for artists; creative enterprise zones; tourism minister; anti‑SLAPP law; gambling levy, ad restrictions, affordability checks; independent football regulator.

- Immigration and asylum: End Hostile Environment; move work/student visa policy out of Home Office; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme; safe/legal routes including humanitarian permits; 3‑month service standard for asylum decisions; lift work ban after 3 months; flexible work visas replacing salary threshold; exemptions for NHS/care workers; expand Youth Mobility; reverse higher family visa thresholds; Windrush redress; repeal Right to Rent; limit detention and ban child detention.

- Rights and democratic reform: Retain Human Rights Act and ECHR; ban conversion practices; digital bill of rights; regulate biometrics; implement Istanbul Convention; votes at 16; proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; cap political donations; Lords reform; written federal constitution; ministerial code in law; stronger transparency and lobbying rules; citizens’ assemblies.

- Defence and international: Increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; parliamentary vote on military action; arms export presumption of denial to human‑rights abusers; procurement reform; better housing/mental health for forces; rebuild EU cooperation via phased roadmap (agencies, MRAs, SPS, Single Market long‑term goal); restore 0.7% aid; support Ukraine (including seizing Russian assets); advocate ceasefire and two‑state process, recognise Palestine; address China/Hong Kong/Uyghurs; fund BBC World Service.

Judge whether A or B aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.
